title: South Austin Sewer Line Construction Greenlit
summary:
*   City leaders approved a major infrastructure project for South Austin.
*   A contract worth $142,897.60 was awarded to Bland Construction Company for the installation of the "South Austin Outfall," a significant sewer line along Riverside Drive.
*   This decision advanced vital utility upgrades, ensuring the expansion of water and sewer services in the growing South Austin area.

The City Manager explained the two methods that could be used, and the recommendation of
the Director of Water Utilities. It was his recommendation also that the contract be
awarded to Bland Construction Company on their low bid.
Councilman Shanks offered the following resolution and moved its adoption (RESOLUTION)
WHEREAS, bids were received by the City of Austin on August 2, 1963, for the installation
of the South Austin Outfall on Riverside Drive from about 650 feet West of East Bouldin
Creek to South First Street; and, WHEREAS, the bid of Bland Construction Company, in the
sum of $142,897.60, was the lowest and best bid therefor, and the acceptance of such bid
has been recommended by the Director of Water and Sewer Department of the City of Austin,
and by the City Manager; Now, Therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
AUSTIN: That the bid of Bland Construction Company, in the sum of $142,897.60, be and the
same is hereby accepted, and that W. T. Williams, Jr., City Manager of the City of Austin,
be and he is hereby authorized to execute a contract, on behalf of the City, with Bland
Construction Company.
The motion, seconded by Councilman Long, carried by the following vote: Ayes:
